e.markdown:
**Diagnosis**
At T+2 min the FDIR event FE-201 fired because the collision probability for Object 58321 (fragmentation debris) exceeded the action threshold: TM-CONJ-02 shows a constant Pc of 0.00021 (2.1 × 10⁻⁴) while the threshold is 1 × 10⁻⁴ [TM-CONJ-02]. The associated conjunction message CDM-0412 predicts a closest approach at T+120 min with a miss distance of 180 m and Pc = 2.1 × 10⁻⁴ [CDM-0412]. Avoidance requires a burn using the 1 N thrusters (P-PROP-04), which must have their catalyst bed pre-heated to 315 °C before firing [TM-CONJ-02.conjunction]. The build record for the heater (P-PROP-05) shows NCR-002: the heater resistance is 52 Ω versus the 46 ± 2 Ω limit, so the bed reaches only 290 °C after 30 min at 12 W and needs about 13 min more to hit 315 °C [NCR-002]. The vehicle flew with this heater dispositioned “Use-as-is under deviation” (asFlown: NCR-002, disposition = Use-as-is under basis that thrusters still reach 315 °C, only slower - about 43.4 min instead of 30 min) [NCR-002].

**Why the build record mattered**
The spec-sheet model assumes a 30 min preheat (REQ-PROP-028) and would allow the burn to start by T+45 min (spec model). Because NCR-002 adds roughly 13 min of preheat, the actual time to reach 315 °C is ~43.4 min, moving the latest viable start-preheat time to T+32 min (as computed by the policy). Without accounting for NCR-002, one would incorrectly think there is ample margin to wait for the operator; the record shows the deadline is tighter and that the operator must decide to start preheat by T+32 min to stay within the avoidance window.

**Public precedent**
WEB-1 notes that monopropellant thrusters require an electric catalyst-bed heater and that a pre-heating time is needed for reliable start, with the elapsed time depending on initial temperature [WEB-1].  
WEB-2 describes integrating the heater into the catalyst bed to improve preheating efficiency and reduce power demand, illustrating why heater resistance affects warm-up time [WEB-2].

**For the operator**
*At the next pass (On-call operator, T+20 min)*  
- Decide whether to start catalyst-bed preheat now (must begin by T+32 min to meet the avoidance deadline).  
- Verify the preheat start command is sent via the GEO data relay (uplink ≤ 1 min).  
- Check remaining Δv budget (≥ 0.075 m/s needed, 130.93 m/s available).  
- Confirm the planned burn lead time (~74.6 min before closest approach) yields a Δv of ~0.075 m/s.

*Afterwards*  
- Monitor thruster temperature (once telemetry for P-PROP-04/05 is available) to confirm the bed reaches ≥ 315 °C before the commanded burn time (~T+45 min).  
- After the burn executes, re-compute collision probability from updated state vectors and verify Pc falls below 1 × 10⁻⁴.  
- Log the actual preheat duration and burn Δv for post-pass analysis and to update future collision-avoidance timings.
